title: India's Private Banks Just Posted Their Strongest Quarter in Over a Year — and Wall Street Is Raising Its Bets
excerpt: HDFC Bank, Axis Bank, and YES Bank report double-digit loan growth in Q1 FY27, lifting the Sensex past 78,200 and extending the market's longest winning streak of 2026
body:
India's private banking heavyweights opened the Q1 FY27 earnings season with a show of strength on Monday, sending the Sensex surging past 78,200 and extending the market's winning streak to four consecutive weeks — its longest of 2026.

HDFC Bank, the country's largest private lender, climbed 3.6 percent after reporting a 15.4 percent year-on-year jump in gross advances to ₹30.61 lakh crore as of June 30. Its deposits crossed ₹31.70 lakh crore, up 14.7 percent. Axis Bank rose 1.7 percent on an even more impressive 18.8 percent growth in gross advances. YES Bank posted 18.4 percent loan growth, while AU Small Finance Bank led the pack at 25.8 percent.

The numbers suggest that India's credit cycle is not just alive — it is accelerating. After a period of caution driven by the Iran war's impact on supply chains and export-facing sectors, the June quarter updates indicate that domestic demand is powering through.

## The Sensex at 78,200: What's Behind the Rally

The benchmark Nifty 50 rose 0.48 percent to 24,385 in early Monday trade, while the Sensex added 0.5 percent to 78,147. By the close, the Sensex had gained 521 points to settle at 78,285, with 12 of 16 major sectors in the green.

Three forces are converging to lift sentiment. First, the bank business updates themselves beat most brokerage estimates. Morgan Stanley noted a "meaningful pickup" in HDFC Bank's year-on-year loan growth and maintained an overweight rating with a ₹1,025 target. Bernstein kept its outperform call at ₹1,150, and Jefferies reiterated buy at ₹1,050.

Second, crude oil prices have dropped sharply on continued U.S.-Iran peace efforts, removing a key headwind for India's current account and corporate margins. Brent crude has retreated more than 20 percent from its recent highs to pre-conflict levels.

Third, foreign portfolio investors are returning. FPIs purchased ₹13.55 billion ($142.3 million) of Indian equities on Friday alone, marking a third consecutive session of net buying. In the bond market, foreign investors have poured a record $3 billion into Indian government bonds in June, attracted by New Delhi's decision to scrap the 12.5 percent long-term capital gains tax and the 20 percent withholding tax on bond interest income.

## Kotak Stumbles, But the Sector Holds

Not every lender shone. Kotak Mahindra Bank fell 3.4 percent after reporting sequential moderation in both loan and deposit growth, even as its year-on-year numbers — 15.1 percent advance growth and 11.7 percent deposit growth — remained respectable.

"Most of the banks which reported June quarter provisional numbers have met or exceeded our estimates, with the exception of Kotak and RBL," said Piran Engineer, senior research analyst at CLSA. The analyst flagged declining CASA ratios across the sector as a margin risk worth watching — HDFC Bank's CASA share slipped to 32.35 percent from 33.90 percent a year ago.

## The Bloomberg Bond Index Factor

Beyond equities, a potentially transformative catalyst is gathering momentum. Bloomberg Index Services, which deferred India's inclusion in its flagship Global Aggregate Bond Index in January, is expected to provide an update in mid-2026. Foreign investors have already bought a net ₹346 billion ($3.6 billion) of government bonds through the Fully Accessible Route since June 1, betting on inclusion.

"A formal inclusion could provide an additional catalyst for foreign inflows in the short term," said Harsimran Sahni, head of treasury at Anand Rathi Global Finance. Analysts estimate phased inflows of $10 billion to $20 billion if the inclusion proceeds — a game-changing sum that would lower India's borrowing costs and strengthen the rupee.

## What NRI Investors Should Watch

For diaspora investors holding Indian bank stocks — among the most popular NRI equity positions — the Q1 updates are broadly encouraging. HDFC Bank's loan growth acceleration from 12 percent in March to 15.4 percent in June signals that the post-merger integration drag is fading. Axis Bank's deposit growth running well above expectations suggests franchise strength.

The risks are real but manageable: the narrowing monsoon deficit (down to 24 percent from 40 percent in late June) should support rural demand, while a potential U.S. rate cut — now more likely after June's soft jobs data — would ease global liquidity conditions further.

Broader market technicals are also constructive. The Nifty is trading above all key moving averages, and the RSI has reclaimed the bullish 60 mark. Analysts at Choice Broking see support at 24,150-24,200 and resistance at 24,400-24,600.

The next test comes when detailed quarterly earnings roll in later this month, revealing whether headline growth has translated into bottom-line strength.

*Sources: Reuters; The Hindu BusinessLine; HDFC Bank, Axis Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank, YES Bank, AU SFB regulatory filings; Morgan Stanley, Bernstein, Jefferies, CLSA research notes; Anand Rathi Global Finance*
